title: Deny Destructive Tool Calls with Agent Control
dataSources: Agent Control decisions on the decorated tool step, recorded as control spans on the request trace
description: Blocks an agent tool call before it runs when its input matches a destructive pattern, using a pre-stage deny control in Splunk Agent Observability Agent Control. The decorated function does not run.
value: Evaluators only report after the fact. A deny control stops the damaging action, such as dropping a table, before it happens, and records the block on the trace.
implementation: Install `agent-control-sdk`, call `agent_control.init`, and decorate the tool with `@control(step_name=...)`. Create a control scoped to that tool step at stage `pre`, with a regex condition on `input` and decision deny. Catch `ControlViolationError` and tell the user the action was refused.
visualization: Control spans (shield icon) on the request traces in the Agent Stream.

references.title: Splunk Agent Observability: Agent Control overview

knownFalsePositives: A broad pattern blocks legitimate requests. Run it as observe first (UC-13.8.28) and read the matches before switching to deny.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback). Agent Control is a separate server and a separate install (`agent-control-sdk`, plus `agent-control-evaluators`; one of those packages is still named `agent-control-evaluator-galileo`, the platform's old name).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

The app calls `agent_control.init` and decorates the step with `@control(step_name=...)`. There are two ways to bind a control, and a tenant uses one of them. The Splunk Agent Observability docs pass the resolved `agent_stream_id` (not the stream name) as `target_id` and attach the control to the stream in the console. The SDK path calls `init(agent_name=...)`, creates a policy, adds the control to it, and assigns the policy to that agent name. If the repo already has an example, follow it. Run the decorated step inside an open trace so the control span lands on that trace.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

A control has a scope (step type `llm` or `tool`, step name, and stage `pre` or `post`), a condition (a selector path such as `input` or `output` plus a check from the control server's catalog: regex, list, JSON, SQL, Luna-2 or custom), and an action. Actions, strictest first: deny, steer, observe; deny wins over steer over observe. Regex patterns are RE2, so there is no lookahead. Write the pattern as the thing to catch: the engine has no "unless". The control server checks its own catalog. It does not run the stream's evaluators, so turning on Tool Selection Quality does not block a bad tool call.

Step 3 — Validate

Send a request that should be denied and one that should pass against a test stream. Confirm the first raises `ControlViolationError`, the function did not run, and a control span appears on the trace. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Keep the control definition in version control next to the tool. Later policy edits need no redeploy; the first integration (`init` plus `@control()`) does.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

Pattern never matches: RE2 has no lookahead, and the engine has no "unless"; rewrite the pattern as the thing to catch. No control span on the trace: the decorated step ran outside an open trace.
grandmaExplanation: Before the assistant does something that could break things, a guard checks the request and stops it if it looks dangerous.

productArtifacts.title: Pre-stage deny control on a database tool
productArtifacts.body:
Scope: step_types=[tool], step_names=[run_sql], stages=[pre]
Condition: selector.path=input; check=regex; pattern=(?i)\b(drop|truncate)\s+table\b (RE2, no lookahead)
Action: decision=deny
Binding: attach to the Agent Stream in the console (target_id = agent_stream_id), or the policy path (init(agent_name=...), create_control, create_policy, add_control_to_policy, assign_policy_to_agent)
Notes: The function does not run when the control denies. If the control server cannot be reached, the call is blocked.
